newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi Arabia and Germany agree to boost trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia and Germany agree to boost trade.

text.p: Saudi Arabia and Germany on Sunday agreed to boost economic, trade, commercial and investment cooperation.
The move was announced in a statement released at the end of a two-day meeting of a German-Saudi joint commission on economic and technical cooperation.

German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt on Saturday called on Saudi Arabia -- Germany's main trading partner in the Arab world -- to improve investment conditions in the kingdom to boost bilateral trade.
In an opening speech of the 12th meeting of the commission in Riyadh, he said German investment in oil giant Saudi Arabia was still modest compared to Germany's other major trading partners.

According to German embassy figures, total bilateral trade between Germany and Saudi Arabia was around 4.8 billion marks ($2.8 billion) in 1995, down from 5.7 billion marks in 1994. In the first nine months of 1996 it stood at 3.7 billion marks.
